title: Saffron Tech — inference pathing & multilingual/tooling scout
summary: Intro call to map Saffron's inference needs: heavy multilingual support, long-context docs, tool-calling for retrieval + external APIs, and strict security/compliance. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, cost/latency targets, KV cache and batching strategies, and pilot plan. Agreed next steps: privacy docs, perf benchmark template, pricing for dedicated pilot, schedule a scoped technical deep-dive.
topics: Model selection (open models vs tuned models)
Context length requirements (50k+ tokens for legal docs)
Tool-calling and retrieval integration (RAG + secure connectors)
Deployment mode tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency
action_items: Ava Moreno: Share Redwood Hosted/Dedicated pricing grid and dedicated pilot SOW by 2027-03-05
Daniel Cho: Send perf-benchmark template and suggested prompt sets by 2027-03-06
Priya Rao: Provide example document set and expected concurrency numbers by 2027-03-08
Carlos Gutierrez: Request Redwood's SOC2 + encryption docs and KMS options by 2027-03-04
Tasha Iverson: Loop in product design for use-case specifics and UX constraints by 2027-03-09
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing & pilot SOW
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) next week to scope benchmarks and telemetry needs
Customer to upload sample docs to secure share for context-length testing
Agree on success metrics for pilot: latency p95 < 500ms for short prompts, end-to-end throughput, and semantic fidelity on multilingual test set
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-02 09:00 PT / Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood Solutions), Liam (Saffron Head of ML), Priya (Platform), Carlos (Security), Tasha (Product), Finance (unidentified)

00:00 - Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ava from redwood, i'll kick us off. can folks introduce quickly?
00:12 - Liam: yeah liam here, head of ml at saffron. our team's evaluating inference paths for a doc assistant product—think legal and compliance workflows, lots of long documents and multilingual inputs.
00:25 - Priya: priya — platform eng — we'll own infra. main asks: predictable latency, cost controls, and tight data controls (no copy to public models).
00:37 - Carlos: carlos, security. SOC2, audit logging, KMS, sso.
00:42 - Ava: great. quick agenda: model selection, context length, multilingual, tool calling (retrieval + external apis), and deployment options. any additions?
00:51 - Tasha: product note — UX needs streaming for user perceived latency, and tool calls for cite generation.
01:03 - Daniel: quick Q up front — are you leaning toward hosted, dedicated, or private? or still exploring?
01:12 - Liam: exploring. initially want hosted for speed, but worried about data residency and certain regulated docs. dedicated or private if we need tighter isolation.
01:22 - Maya: ok noted. tell us about the document sizes and context window requirements.
01:30 - Liam: average doc is 12k tokens, but we often need cross-document context across 6–8 docs, so realistic working context 60–100k tokens. can't chop context too much, loses legal reasoning.
01:45 - Daniel: got it — 60–100k is large, that pushes us toward models with extended context support or chunking + strong RAG. how are you thinking about tool-calling — synchronous calls to internal APIs or async pipelines?
01:57 - Tasha: mostly synchronous, user hits a button, we call retrieval + citation generator + internal vetting rule engine. end-to-end should be subsecond for short queries and under 5s for deep doc reasoning ideally.
02:12 - Priya: concurrency: initial 10–20 qps, but could spike to 100 qps in peak. budget sensitivity — want a path that keeps unit token cost reasonable.
02:26 - Daniel: ok — cost vs latency tradeoff. Redwood can host optimized kernels and batch efficiently; dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost per token, private gives full isolation but more ops.
02:40 - Liam: what's the open-model story? we prefer OSS model family if quality holds; don't want to be locked to a proprietary stack.
02:49 - Ava: we maintain a model catalog — open models with verified perf. for 100k context you have a few choices: long-context Llama derivatives, locally-extended models, or LLamaX-style architectures; sometimes we use hybrid: KV cache + chunked encoder + cross-doc retrieval.
03:07 - Liam: could you name specific model candidates? we want to evaluate tradeoffs.
03:12 - Daniel: examples — Llama2-Chat-extended, Mistral-Long variants, Mixtral extended-context forks, and Redford-clarity (internal name, we mentioned a tuned variant). note: names sometimes transcribed wrong — we also benchmark open longformer-ish forks.
03:32 - Priya: tokenization differences across languages worry us — especially for east-asian locales and right-to-left scripts. Any known regressions?
03:41 - Maya: yes tokenization can blow up token count for some asian langs, we recommend measuring with your corpora. also apply per-language quantization profiles.
03:52 - Tasha: for multilingual quality, we need parity across en/es/ja/ko/fr. is fine-tuning or instruction-tuning required?
04:02 - Daniel: depends on fidelity needs. for citation/precise extraction, instruction-tuning + small task-specific tuning helps; for pure summarization, zero-shot with prompts sometimes ok but less consistent.
04:19 - Carlos: security: can we host in VPC and have customer-owned KMS? also need audit logs for all API calls and redaction controls.
04:28 - Ava: yes — private deployment offers customer-managed control plane in their VPC and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Dedicated supports VPC peering and brings most of the controls, with logs shipped to your SIEM. Hosted can be configured for tenancy and retention but may not meet air-gapped requirements.
04:48 - Liam: latency numbers — you mentioned p95 targets?
04:52 - Daniel: for short prompts on dedicated we typically hit p95 ~150–350ms depending on model and hardware; hosted varies but we publish ranges. long context generation depends on decoding length and compute — long context at scale will be multiple seconds; heavy KV cache and prefix cache can help repeated context.
05:12 - Priya: how do you handle KV cache / recurrent contexts? transcription sometimes says K V cache as kay vee — apologies.
05:20 - Daniel: we do prefix caching, slice-level KV caching, and can pin context shards in memory for dedicated customers. caching reduces repeated token compute, but introduces cache invalidation complexity.
05:35 - Liam: can caching be shared across tenants?
05:38 - Maya: no, for dedicated/private it's per-customer. hosted there's dedup opportunities but we don't serve raw customer data to others.
05:48 - Tasha: tool-calling — do you support function-call style hooks and structured outputs?
05:54 - Ava: yes, we support streaming responses with tool-call hooks; you can define typed function schemas, and the runtime can call out to your secure connectors. we also support reranking and safety filters.
06:06 - Priya: connectors — any out-of-the-box connectors to enterprise docs stores (sharepoint, confluence)?
06:12 - Maya: we have prebuilt connectors for common stores and a secure connector framework for custom sources.
06:18 - Liam: for the pilot, we want to run a benchmark: accuracy on citation, multilingual fidelity, latency p95, and cost per session. what does Redwood typically include in a perf bench?
06:29 - Daniel: lab bench includes standardized prompt sets, language variants, synthetic long-context stress tests, and concurrency load. we also do end-to-end tests with your retrieval layer. we'll give a template for your docs + prompt sets.
06:42 - Tasha: what about quantization — int8 vs int4? will that materially change quality on long-context?
06:50 - Daniel: int8 is usually safe for many sizes; int4 can reduce memory but may degrade quality for sensitive legal phrasing. we recommend running A/B on your tasks; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
07:05 - Priya: cost model — how is dedicated priced? committed throughput?
07:10 - Ava: dedicated is monthly reserved capacity with committed vGPU pools; pricing depends on instance type, throughput, and run hours. we'll share a grid. hosted is pay-as-you-go per-token with tiers; private is licensing + ops.
07:26 - Finance (unid): quick Q — what are minimum commitments?
07:29 - Ava: depends — we can design a 3-month pilot with limited commit. we'll share SOW templates.
07:36 - Liam: do you have region coverage — we need eu + apac for data residency.
07:40 - Maya: yes hosted has regions, dedicated can be provisioned in preferred regions, and private obviously can be installed on-prem/apac cloud.
07:49 - Carlos: how are logs handled for audit — full request/response or redacted?
07:54 - Ava: logs can be configured; for sensitive workloads we support redaction, token-level cost traces, and shipping to your SIEM. audit trails include model version, prompt hash (optionally redacted), and outcome.
08:10 - Priya: what's the integration effort for SSO/SAML and RBAC?
08:14 - Maya: straightforward — SAML, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access. we'll share sample configs.
08:22 - Liam: can we run a brief mental test — suppose a user submits a 70k token allegation packet in japanese plus related english exhibits. we need cross-lang reasoning and cite generation. what's the recommended path?
08:36 - Daniel: approach A: use an extended-context model that natively supports 70k tokens — simplest but potentially costly. Approach B: chunk + RAG with semantic retrieval and cross-doc alignment (store embeddings, retrieve relevant windows, and perform constrained cross-attention); combine with tool-call for citation generator. A hybrid: use long-context model for session-level reasoning when available and fallback to RAG on spikes.
09:03 - Tasha: fallback behavior — if long model fails or there's capacity pressure, can Redwood automatically degrade to a smaller model or queued mode?
09:13 - Ava: yes policy routing — we can route by latency SLO or cost policy. automatic fallback to compatible smaller variants or cached responses.
09:22 - Liam: training/fine-tuning — do you offer managed fine-tune?
09:26 - Maya: we offer managed tuning for enterprise customers on dedicated/private, plus guidance for prompt engineering. For hosted we have limited fine-tune capabilities with privacy controls.
09:37 - Priya: instrumentation — how granular is cost telemetry? token-level? per-route? session-level?
09:43 - Daniel: token-level breakdown, per-route and per-model dashboards, and traces you can hook into.
09:50 - Carlos: encryption in transit and at rest? HSM options?
09:53 - Ava: TLS in transit, at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS for private/dedicated; HSM integrations supported for private deployments.
10:05 - Liam: timelines — if we do a 6-week pilot, what does Redwood need from us?
10:11 - Daniel: sample datasets, success metrics, concurrency numbers, and acceptance criteria. we provision dedicated capacity for benching; pilot SOW covers infra and support.
10:20 - Tasha: UX question — streaming latency with tool-calls when multiple tools invoked sequentially?
10:26 - Daniel: streaming works while the model decides and calls tools; if the model awaits an external sync call, UX can show interim streaming tokens and spinner for external step. overall we design for partial streaming and optimistic UI.
10:41 - Priya: any regulatory concerns for PII in logs?
10:44 - Ava: we recommend redaction and using token-level hashing; we can implement PII filters and avoid persistent storage of raw PD.
10:54 - Liam: competition — we looked at Anthropic and some cloud offerings. why choose Redwood?
11:00 - Ava: our value prop is production-first inference across hosted/dedicated/private, smart routing, and cost controls with observability. we glue model ops and infra with a dev-friendly API.
11:12 - Tasha: can you do a short handoff to the SE team for deeper perf scoping?
11:16 - Ava: absolutely — daniel will lead the technical deep-dive.
11:19 - Daniel: next step from SE side, we'll send the perf template and propose dates for benching. also want to sync on multilingual tokenizer stats.
11:28 - Priya: we'll prepare corpora and point you to a secure share.
11:34 - Carlos: security will review your SOC2 and encryption docs. send those asap.
11:40 - Liam: final — success metrics again? latency, citation accuracy, multilingual F1, and cost per session.
11:49 - Ava: noted, we'll include those as suggested metrics in the SOW.
11:55 - Tasha: any blockers from Redwood perspective?
11:58 - Maya: none — just need your sample docs and to agree on pilot dates.
12:05 - Ava: wrap up, thanks all — we'll send pricing, SOW, perf template, and security pack. catch you next week.
12:12 - Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and model variants may be mis-transcribed (e.g., Mixtral, Redford-clarity). There were a few crosstalk moments during the latency discussion.
notes: Customer strongly focused on 60-100k token joint context and synchronous tool-calling. Preference for open models but with enterprise controls. Agreed pilot scope and deliverables.
duration_one_line: 58 minutes — fairly technical discovery with AE+SE and security presence
